The 2017 Wikipedia dump 2.0 used (gensim wiki-english-20171001) has templates stripped: no infoboxes (5 of 20,000 sampled articles mention one). Wikimedia/Wikidata/DBpedia/archive.org are unreachable. Infobox facts come from WikiBio (728K Wikipedia biography infoboxes, enwiki 2015-09, CC BY-SA 3.0, on GitHub) instead; lead sentences still come from the 2017 dump.

Structured tables: mledoze/countries (ODbL), countryinfo (MIT, populations ~2015), geonamescache 3.0.2 (MIT/GeoNames CC BY 4.0, cities >=15K), us (BSD-3), periodictable (public domain), airportsdata (MIT), goodbooks-10k (CC BY-SA 4.0), planets hand table (moon counts as of 2023).
2026 overlay: 106 hand-written facts (leaders, populations, records) from Claude's knowledge, not externally verified.

Index: the sparse index is BM25-style word postings over entity names/aliases (plus exact sorted-name/alias binary search), not over full fact text; a fact-text BM25 index like 2.0's costs ~3.2 MB per 100K facts and cannot fit 500K facts in 8 MB.
Fact rendering (ISO date -> 'march 14, 1879', digits -> '66,078,000') is done by fact storage when evidence is shown to the model; it never chooses an answer.
Precision check judged by Claude (the builder); one round failed (98.5%) and the responsible extractors were fixed before the passing round (99.2%).

Test re-frozen (same seed, same generator) after fixing a nondeterministic KB build: NLTK returns multiple hypernyms in hash-dependent order and the WordNet is-a choice took the first one; hypernyms are now sorted by name. The overlay's office-holder facts were also set to 'as of 2026' (their check date). No training had happened; the partial 2.0 baseline on the first freeze was discarded.

Trigram feature hash changed from md5 to an integer hash Scratch computes exactly (engine/tok.py tri_bucket), before any real training; a lookup table would have dropped unseen trigrams of typos and broken parity.
Scratch's timer block reads runtime.currentMSecs (updated once per frame), so chunk budgets use 'days since 2000' (wall clock) instead.

TurboWarp compiles a script on first run (~0.16-0.2 s for one script holding everything). The engine is split into 3 worker scripts (turn driver, model kernels, 2.0 tools) that the green flag starts once each on separate frames so each compiles in its own frame; this is the only green-flag work besides resetting state.

Test generator bug: 2,469 derived items (capital of the country of a city/airport) had gold=null because some capitals are stored as plain text. Fixed in the gold computation only (no RNG change); questions unchanged; test re-generated and re-frozen before training.
Executor fixes found while porting: ISA_FN was never set (isa tool would crash); 8-digit date with month 00 guard (no such facts exist; kept for safety).
Python mirror and Scratch cap a turn at 500 positions and 150 user tokens; /reset and /help are handled before the model in both.
decisions: Weights stored as 2-digit decimal strings with QAT (~0.7 deflated bytes/weight at 32 levels vs 1.24 for 2.0's int8 list items); decode costs ~2.8x compute.

Engine = one small decoder ('brain') with a copy pointer that reads the question, issues lookups/tool calls, picks candidates, decides answer/fallback/clarify and writes every word; candidates come from the non-learned name index.
KB quota: persons 82K (WikiBio), leads 30K (2017), WordNet 25K senses (+is-a closure), all table entities.
Weights: per-row 2-digit codes (value = (code-49)*scale), dot products as sum(code*x) - 49*sum(x).
Work units ~1 ms; a chunk runs units for <= 3.5 ms wall time (cap 200 units).
kb_cmd: Q_PERSONS=80000 Q_LEADS=30000 Q_WORDNET=25000 python3 kb/merge.py && POST_CAP=80 python3 kb/encode.py
